Speaker's Card/Request to Speak: If you would like to address the City Council on a scheduled agenda item, including a Consent Calendar item, a Regular Council Business item, a Public Hearing item, or Public Comments, please complete the "Request to Speak Form." The card is at the table at the entrance to the City Council Chamber. Please identify on the card your name and the item on which you would like to speak and return to the City Clerk. The "Request to Speak Form" assists the Mayor in ensuring that all persons wishing to address the City Council are recognized. It also ensures the accurate identification of meeting participants in the City Council minutes. Your name will be called at the time the matter is heard by the City Council. City policy is to limit public testimony to up to three minutes per speaker depending on relevant circumstances (unless the time limit is extended by the Mayor), which includes the presentation of electronic or audio visual information. Speakers may not yield their time to other persons.
Please take notice that the order of scheduled agenda items below and/or the time they are actually heard, considered and decided may be modified by the Mayor or the City Council during the course of the meeting, so please stay alert.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk''s Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us . Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City''s system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:
 City Clerk's Office

 Front Entrance of City Hall
 University Park Center (Culver/Michelson)
 Walnut Village Center (Culver/Walnut)
 Northwood Town Center (Irvine Blvd./Yale)
 City's web page at www.ci.irvine.ca.us

November 12, 2019, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center
Plaza, Irvine, California; Mayor Shea presiding.

  RECESS

  Mayor Shea recessed the City Council meeting to Closed Session at 4:10 p.m.

  RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  Mayor Shea reconvened the City Council meeting at 5:37 p.m. City Attorney Melching,
  on behalf of the City Council, announced that no reportable action was taken in Closed

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Pro Tempore Kuo led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  November 12, 2019

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Mike Anderson from Good Shepherd Lutheran Church in Irvine provided the
  invocation.

  2.  PRESENTATIONS

  2.1  Proclaim Sikh Awareness and Appreciation Month

  Mayor Shea introduced Avinder Chawla, Transportation Commissioner,
  and Councilmember Khan presented him with a proclamation recognizing
  November 2019 as “Sikh Awareness and Appreciation Month.”

  2.2  Evacuation Plan Overview

  Bobby Simmons, Emergency Management Administrator, provided an
  overview of the City’s Evacuation Plan.

  City Council discussion included: expressing concern related to evacuation
  management during the 1993 Laguna Canyon Fire; referenced the recent
  power outage at a Southern California Edison substation on Jamboree and
  Michelson and related communication concerns; questioned why the
  University of California, Irvine (UCI) was exempted from Irvine’s evacuation
  zones; and inquired about how the City would coordinate with UCI during
  an emergency evacuation.

  2.3  Drone Team Update

  Mayor Shea introduced Tim Schilling, Police Lieutenant, and Chris Bees,
  Police Sergeant, who provided an update on the Irvine Police Department’s
  Drone Team.

  City Council discussion included: questioning whether a drone would
  perform similarly to Orange County Fire Authority’s emergency helicopter
  but at a significant cost reduction; and inquired about how City of Irvine
  drones would be used for emergency events outside of the City.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  November 12, 2019

  2.4  Implementation of Senate Bill 245

  Mayor Shea introduced Mike Cribbin, Manager of Community Services,
  who provided an update on the implementation of Senate Bill 245 (“Pets for
  Vets Act”).

  City Council discussion included: questioning types of acceptable
  identification other than a driver’s license to verify the identity of veterans;
  and inquired about the Irvine Animal Care Center’s upcoming “Home for
  the Holidays” event.

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  John Russo, City Manager, turned to Mike Hamel, Police Chief, who introduced Orange
  County Fire Authority’s new Division Chief, Shane Sherwood.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Carroll, as the City’s delegate to the Southern California Association of
  Governments (SCAG) Board of Directors, provided a brief update on the most recent
  Board meeting, noting last-minute changes that were reviewed and approved by the
  Board with respect to the allocation of Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA)
  units.

  Councilmember Khan expressed her appreciation to the City Council, staff, residents,
  and organizations that attended the last City Council meeting to support the adoption of
  the City’s updated Smoking Ordinance; and made the following announcements:

  •  The Make A Wish Foundation recently welcomed its new President and Chief
  Executive Officer, Gloria Crockett, at an event in which Councilmember Khan
  attended, and at the event, attendees were asked to write letters from Santa, to
  be delivered to the Foundation or Macy’s as each letter would generate a
  contribution of $1 by Macy’s. Community members are also invited to participate.
  Letters can be dropped off at Macy’s or the Make A Wish Foundation.

  •  On Friday, November 16 at 9 a.m., Chairwoman Khan, along with the Orange
  County Great Park Board of Directors, will be attending the opening of the new
  playground at the Great Park next to the Visitors Center.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  November 12, 2019

  Mayor Shea made the following announcements:

  •  The community is invited to join the City of Irvine and the Irvine 2/11 Marine
  Adoption Committee in brightening the season for military families by participating
  in the annual Holiday Toy Drive underway now through December 13. This
  community effort supports the families of Irvine’s adopted 2/11 Marine Battalion.
  Donation bins for unwrapped gifts suitable for infants or children up to 12 years of
  age are located at City Hall, the Irvine Police Department, and the Orange County
  Great Park Visitors Center.

  •  In order to better prepare in advance of a natural disaster, the City is developing a
  Local Hazard Mitigation Plan, which will help identify those situations, assess the
  City’s current provisions, and outline a strategy to lessen the vulnerability and
  severity of future disasters. The City is asking the community to help by
  completing a brief Local Hazard Mitigation Plan survey available on the City’s
  website at cityofirvine.org.

  •  The Institute for Local Government selected the City of Irvine as a 2019 Beacon
  Sustainability Spotlight award winner. The Beacon Program supports and
  recognizes voluntary action by local governments throughout California to address
  climate change, promote energy innovation, and create more sustainable
  communities. The City of Irvine received the award for efforts to reduce electricity
  and natural gas consumption at the City’s municipal facilities, and also received
  the top platinum level award in the Sustainability Best Practices category in
  recognition of the City’s robust environmental programs that have been
  incorporated agency wide.

  •  The community is invited to attend the 38th Annual Irvine Community
  Thanksgiving Prayer Breakfast on Thursday, November 21, at the Irvine Marriott
  Hotel. The keynote speaker will be former LA Rams football player Reggie Doss.
  He and his wife, Tamara, are founders of Amazing Life Ministries, which
  advocates for fostering and adopting at-risk children. Tickets are $50, with
  proceeds benefitting The Raise Foundation, which is dedicated to preventing and
  stopping the cycle of child abuse.

  •  Parenting OC magazine readers named Heritage Community Park “Best
  Playground” for the sixth consecutive year. Last month, the State Auditor’s Office
  created a comprehensive ranking of California cities based on fiscal health and
  Irvine was assessed as “low risk.” In comparison, many neighboring cities in
  Orange County were listed as “moderate risk.” City of Irvine residents have given
  Irvine very high marks in a recent Quality of Life survey sponsored by the Greater
  Irvine Chamber.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5
 City Council Minutes  November 12, 2019

  •  On November 1, a banner messaging “Reclaim America” was placed on a
  California Interstate 405 overpass by an organization known as “Patriot Front,” a
  Neo-Nazi organization. Mike Hamel, Chief of Police, was contacted and the Irvine
  Police Department took immediate action in removing the sign. The City Council
  has made it clear that Irvine does not want nor tolerate this type of banner, or any
  type of discrimination, in the City.

  4.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  4.1  ON-DEMAND MOBILE FUELING OPERATIONS  UPDATE  AND
  PROPOSED MUNICIPAL CODE AMENDMENTS

  Mayor Shea opened the public hearing at 7:17p p.m.

  Kyle Turner, Police Lieutenant, and Jennifer Bower, Orange County Fire
  Authority Deputy Fire Marshal, presented the staff report and responded to
  questions.

  City Council discussion included: inquiring about whether business licenses
  for this type of program would be limited; questioned whether we could
  require Booster to be based in Irvine to capture sales tax revenue; inquired
  about whether sales tax would be based on point of generation; questioned
  whether any incidents have occurred as part of the pilot program similar to
  other areas; expressed concern about unlocked fuel tanks in vehicles and
  potential vandalism that could ensue, and whether any technology existed
  to avoid such vandalism; questioned whether diesel fuel was an option;
  suggested more frequent updates regarding status of the program; inquired
  about other jurisdictions in which Booster has delivered to; and questioned
  whether mobile fueling was limited to personal vehicles or included
  commercial/fleet mobile fuel delivery.

  Taylor Henderson, representing Booster Fuels, provided a brief overview of
  the services provided, and spoke in support of the Ordinance.

  ACTION:  Moved by Mayor Shea, seconded by Mayor Pro Tempore
  Kuo, and unanimously carried to close the public hearing at 7:31 p.m.

  ACTION:  Moved by Mayor Pro Tempore Kuo, seconded by
  Councilmember Khan, and unanimously carried to:

  Introduce for first reading and read by title only ORDINANCE NO.
  19-18 – AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING SECTION 5-9-408 OF
  CHAPTER 4 OF DIVISION 9 OF TITLE 5 OF THE IRVINE
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO REGULATION OF ON-DEMAND
  MOBILE FUELING OPERATIONS

  ACTION:  Moved by Mayor  Pro  Tempore  Kuo,  seconded  by
  Councilmember Khan, to:

  Direct staff to continue monitoring mobile fueling activity and provide
  a written update to City Council in 24 months.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  10
 City Council Minutes  November 12, 2019

  Discussion ensued related to suggesting more frequent updates to the City
  Council on mobile fueling activity.

  ACTION: A friendly amendment was made by Mayor Shea, and
  accepted by Mayor Pro Tempore Kuo as the maker of the motion and
  Councilmember Khan as the seconder, and unanimously carried to:

  Direct staff to continue monitoring mobile fueling activity and provide
  a written update to City Council in 6, 12, and 24 month increments.
